cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, gets a message from the LORD for the Israelites about a special vow: the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD. Friend, this is not a casual promise. This is a COMMITMENT.

cards.question: Who can make the special vow of a Nazirite?

cards.text: Rule number one is about the grapevine. A Nazirite is to abstain from wine and strong drink, and even vinegar made from them.

cards.question: Grape juice and raisins are still fine for a Nazirite, since there's no wine in them.

cards.text: "All the days of his separation, he is not to eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or skins." That's like swearing off cookies and then finding out the crumbs count too. The CRUMBS, friend.
Rule number two is about his head. For the entire period of the vow, one thing stays away from it.

cards.question: For the entire period of the vow, no ___ shall touch the Nazirite's head.

cards.text: So his hair grows long, and he must be holy until his time of separation to the LORD is complete. Don't look at my mustache, friend. I KNOW.
Rule number three, and friend, this one's no joke. Throughout the days of his separation to the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.

cards.question: What if the Nazirite's own father or mother dies during the vow?

answers.text: He still stays away from the body
He may go near just that once
He must prepare the body himself

cards.question: Why does the Nazirite stay away, even from his own family?

answers.text: The symbol of consecration is on his head
His family would be put to shame
His tribe would lose its blessing

cards.text: Throughout his separation, he is holy to the LORD. But if someone suddenly dies right there in his presence, his consecrated head of hair is defiled.

cards.question: When a sudden death defiles a Nazirite's hair, what must he do on his day of cleansing?
The Nazirite's day of cleansing comes on the ___ day.

cards.text: Day eight, he's back at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting with two turtledoves or two young pigeons for the priest. One's a sin offering, one's a burnt offering, and atonement is made for him.

cards.question: On that same day, the Nazirite has to consecrate his head all over again.

cards.text: Then he rededicates his time of separation to the LORD and brings a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. And now the question I'd be SWEATING over: what about all the days he already put in?

cards.question: What happens to the days of the vow the Nazirite already finished before the dead body?

answers.text: They count toward the new vow

cards.text: Now the happy part, friend: the FINISH LINE. When the Nazirite's time of separation is complete, he's brought to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

Then the offerings come, and they just KEEP coming: an unblemished male lamb, female lamb and ram, with grain and drink offerings and a basket of unleavened cakes and wafers. The priest presents all these before the LORD.

cards.question: Right there at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, what does the Nazirite do with his consecrated head?
After the shave, the Nazirite puts his hair on the ___ under the peace offering.

cards.text: All those days of growing go right on the fire, and friend, I can't toss out ONE burnt cookie without a moment of silence. Then the priest puts the ram's shoulder, a cake and a wafer in the Nazirite's hands and waves them before the LORD as a holy portion for the priest.

cards.question: After all of this, the Nazirite may drink wine.

cards.text: Then the LORD sums it up: this is the law of the Nazirite, and his offering comes in addition to whatever else he can afford. One last line, friend, and it's the BIG one.

cards.question: Whatever vow a Nazirite makes, what must he do with it?
